subject: tipsy tooltips on a d3 chart

messages.author: 7d2a96af532ed7de
messages.subject: tipsy tooltips on a d3 chart
parts:
Hey Folks,

Once again, thanks so much for shiny, and for gracefully dealing with my inane questions! I must make the usual apology and disclaimer that I'm very woefully inexperienced with every piece of technology which I'm trying to use.

I'd like to make a scatter chart in d3, with tooltips that contain links. I'd like to bind events to the links, so that the app might whisk the user to a new tab with some more detailed information on the data point in question.

So far I've got to a minimal Frankenexample from Jeff's nets, and Kenton's Bars, with the addition of jdonaldson's tipsy tooltips.

I've fallen at the first hurdle, which is making tipsy render svg titles when the visual is hosted via shiny. I can get it going on a static page (here, ignore the nonsense labels).

Via shiny, the svg elements do have the right titles as defined in d3 (in the usual postit coloured boxes), but they don't have controllable tipsy behaviours or styles. My instinct was that the tipsy css/js wasn't loading (as far as I can tell from looking at my browser's GET requests, it is), or that a tiny bit of js (to set and 'activate' the tipsy options) wasn't running (I tested this by defining a variable inside it, and seeing if it was retrievable from my browser, which it was).

So, my guess is that either the reading of the tipsy js, css, or the in-code .js which sets it's options are being read in the wrong place. Unfortunately I have no idea where the right place is. Currently they're read in as part of graph.js. Attempts to get it between <head> tags have killed the app altogether.

Hopefully this is trivial to someone who understands the DOM... Any ideas?

Brendan

P.S.
The app's on GH ( runGitHub("shiny-d3-scatter","brendan-R") ).

messages.author: 7d2a96af532ed7de
messages.subject: Re: tipsy tooltips on a d3 chart
parts:
Apologies Joe, I got the tooltips rendering last thing on Friday, quickly synched to GH, and forgot to repost! Excited bout the libraries. If you guys have any code sitting around that does somthing like this, or you've had luck with an alternative approach, I'd be keen to hear about it!

I've got a little closer to producing links which have the desired behaviours (or at least, bootstrap buttons that look like links). I can get them working fine sitting on the UI, but they don't seem to speak to the server once they're embedded in tipsy.

The method I used to get them in there was pretty blunt; I just made graph.js paste the HTML to produce a button into the svg title for each point. I've tried them within and without divs (and tried the naming the divs the same and differently to the divs shiny produces), but without any luck.

e.g., here's the R/shiny server code to generate the buttons

pointLink <- function(d){
    # The function which actionButton() calls
    tags$button(
        id = paste0("point_lnk_",d$id),
        type = "button",
        class = "btn action-button btn-link",
        d$name
    )
}

Run over the dataset, and returned as a tagList, rendered in ui.R with uiOutput("pla").
I then grepl the click counts out of the input list, to make things happen.

and here's the .js
...rest of d3 code...
  .append("svg:title")
    .text(function(d) {
        return ''
        +'<div id="pla" class="shiny-html-output shiny-bound-output">'
        +'<button id="point_lnk_' + d.id + '" class="btn action-button btn-link shiny-bound-input" type="button">' + d.lab +'</button>'
        + '</div>'
        });

Any ideas if I'm along the right lines? Or why it's not working? I suspect that the buttons may be too deep in the DOM for shiny to find them, but I'm on the edge of my paltry understanding!

Apologies that these aren't really shiny specific questions, but hopefully this is a commonish use-case, and of interest to others trying to get similar things going!

messages.subject: Re: tipsy tooltips on a d3 chart
parts:
Rather than have those tooltips contain action buttons, I think it'd be much more straightforward to have them contain regular links whose javascript event handlers simply set a Shiny input value directly. There is a (not currently documented, but we're most likely going to keep supporting it indefinitely) function "Shiny.onInputChange(name, value)" that you can call from JS, and in server.R, input$name will reflect that change and reactivity will be triggered, etc.

(You appear to have the d3/JS chops to take it from there, but if not, let me know and I will try to help connect the dots for you...)
